k: Best pickpocket in Aurenne. Ask anyone.
src: 'Best pickpocket in Aurenne. Ask anyone.'

k: Eleven and three-quarters
src: 'Eleven and three-quarters'

k: Sky-pirate. Gambler. Charming coward.
src: 'Sky-pirate. Gambler. Charming coward.'

k: Captain of the Halcyon
src: 'Captain of the Halcyon'

k: The kindest man in the world.
src: 'The kindest man in the world.'

k: “Every child wants the good days never to end.”
src: '“Every child wants the good days never to end.”'

k: _One Crest, one life_ — or so they say.
src: '_One Crest, one life_ — or so they say.'

k: Where the trees remember
src: 'Where the trees remember'

k: Dunes of glass
src: 'Dunes of glass'

k: The Greyspine Mountains
src: 'The Greyspine Mountains'

k: An island above the storm
src: 'An island above the storm'

k: BREAK!
src: 'BREAK!'

k: Then, one sunset, the sun stopped.
src: 'Then, one sunset, the sun stopped.'

k: —and broke into seven pieces.
src: '—and broke into seven pieces.'

k: One year later
src: 'One year later'

k: What was left of the world
src: 'What was left of the world'

k: Children of the wreck
src: 'Children of the wreck'

k: Wings, again
src: 'Wings, again'

k: “Stay. Here, the good days never end.”
src: '“Stay. Here, the good days never end.”'

k: A coming-of-age at the end of the world
src: 'A coming-of-age at the end of the world'

k: If you see a little golden light flitting about down there — a Wishing Mote — use magic. Blades go right through it. Catch one and it might leave a Crest Tome.
src: 'If you see a little golden light flitting about down there — a Wishing Mote — use magic. Blades go right through it. Catch one and it might leave a Crest Tome.'

k: The chests down there that bite are Hoarder Mimics. They've eaten whole fortunes. Pierce them, shock them, and they cough up the most wonderful fruit.
src: 'The chests down there that bite are Hoarder Mimics. They\'ve eaten whole fortunes. Pierce them, shock them, and they cough up the most wonderful fruit.'

k: Every fifth stair has a Hearthstone. Somebody put them there. I would very much like to meet that somebody.
src: 'Every fifth stair has a Hearthstone. Somebody put them there. I would very much like to meet that somebody.'

k: You beat YOURSELVES. Dace cried. Not the happy kind — he had money on the hollow ones. I didn't. I'm rich. Four coppers rich.
src: 'You beat YOURSELVES. Dace cried. Not the happy kind — he had money on the hollow ones. I didn\'t. I\'m rich. Four coppers rich.'

k: The Colosseum's through that big door. Dace'll fight you against anything the Gloam remembers. Everything you ever beat, it remembers.
src: 'The Colosseum\'s through that big door. Dace\'ll fight you against anything the Gloam remembers. Everything you ever beat, it remembers.'

k: Chalk on the stone in a child's hand: a hopscotch grid, and beside it — I'M HIDING. DON'T LOOK HERE. (She was not hiding here.)
src: 'Chalk on the stone in a child\'s hand: a hopscotch grid, and beside it — I\'M HIDING. DON\'T LOOK HERE. (She was not hiding here.)'

k: A chalk arrow, pointing the way she went. Underneath: WARMER!
src: 'A chalk arrow, pointing the way she went. Underneath: WARMER!'

k: Chalk, faded but careful: CASSIAN ALWAYS FINDS ME. HE'S THE BEST AT THIS GAME. Below it, very small: are you cassian?
src: 'Chalk, faded but careful: CASSIAN ALWAYS FINDS ME. HE\'S THE BEST AT THIS GAME. Below it, very small: are you cassian?'

k: A chalk door, drawn small, rubbed out, and drawn again bigger. Under it: I GOT TIRED OF WAITING. I'M SOMEWHERE NICE NOW. THE DOOR IS WHERE IT STARTED.
src: 'A chalk door, drawn small, rubbed out, and drawn again bigger. Under it: I GOT TIRED OF WAITING. I\'M SOMEWHERE NICE NOW. THE DOOR IS WHERE IT STARTED.'

k: "Warmer! Warmer!"
src: '"Warmer! Warmer!"'

k: "Cold!"
src: '"Cold!"'

k: "Freezing! Brrr!"
src: '"Freezing! Brrr!"'

k: In the world of Solmere, the sun sets into the Western Sea every evening.
src: 'In the world of Solmere, the sun sets into the Western Sea every evening.'

k: Every dawn, the Seven Lanterns sing it back into the sky.
src: 'Every dawn, the Seven Lanterns sing it back into the sky.'

k: And every child, at sixteen, stands in a Lantern's light to receive a Crest —
src: 'And every child, at sixteen, stands in a Lantern\'s light to receive a Crest —'

k: the calling they will carry for the rest of their life.
src: 'the calling they will carry for the rest of their life.'

k: _One Crest. One life._
src: '_One Crest. One life._'

k: That is how it has always been.
src: 'That is how it has always been.'

k: I was reading.
src: 'I was reading.'

k: Until dawn. _Again._ Tomorrow you stand in the Lantern's light. You could at least do it with your eyes open.
src: 'Until dawn. _Again._ Tomorrow you stand in the Lantern\'s light. You could at least do it with your eyes open.'

k: The Hierophant's ship comes in today, doesn't it? Ilse says he's coming himself. For _our_ Kindling.
src: 'The Hierophant\'s ship comes in today, doesn\'t it? Ilse says he\'s coming himself. For _our_ Kindling.'

k: ...He is.
src: '...He is.'

k: Mom. He's the _Hierophant_. He wrote back to me. Twice.
src: 'Mom. He\'s the _Hierophant_. He wrote back to me. Twice.'

k: I know. I read them.
src: 'I know. I read them.'

k: You read my—
src: 'You read my—'

k: Chores. Tobias needs his net back from Nana Brisa's. After that you can go and gawk at the harbor with everyone else.
src: 'Chores. Tobias needs his net back from Nana Brisa\'s. After that you can go and gawk at the harbor with everyone else.'

k: Some mothers would be proud their daughter writes to the most important man in the world.
src: 'Some mothers would be proud their daughter writes to the most important man in the world.'

k: The day before the Kindling. The Hierophant himself is coming to Lanternfall. Mom read my letters.
src: 'The day before the Kindling. The Hierophant himself is coming to Lanternfall. Mom read my letters.'

k: Supper soon. Wash the sea out of your hair first.
src: 'Supper soon. Wash the sea out of your hair first.'

k: The tide caves? ...Of course you are.
src: 'The tide caves? ...Of course you are.'

k: Take Ilse. Stay out of the deep pools. And Wren — the tide comes back faster than you think.
src: 'Take Ilse. Stay out of the deep pools. And Wren — the tide comes back faster than you think.'

k: Nana Brisa's house is the plaster one by the square. Red roof.
src: 'Nana Brisa\'s house is the plaster one by the square. Red roof.'

k: And don't let Tobias talk you into gutting fish. Not today.
src: 'And don\'t let Tobias talk you into gutting fish. Not today.'

k: You're late.
src: 'You\'re late.'

k: I'm _exactly_ on time for someone who was reading.
src: 'I\'m _exactly_ on time for someone who was reading.'

k: Wren, dear! Tobias's net is by the fire. Mended with my best knots — tell him that.
src: 'Wren, dear! Tobias\'s net is by the fire. Mended with my best knots — tell him that.'

k: If only everything mended so easily...
src: 'If only everything mended so easily...'

k: Nana lost her brooch. The silver gull Grandpa gave her.
src: 'Nana lost her brooch. The silver gull Grandpa gave her.'

k: In the tide caves, years ago. I was gathering sea lavender and it simply... went into the water. I've made my peace with it.
src: 'In the tide caves, years ago. I was gathering sea lavender and it simply... went into the water. I\'ve made my peace with it.'

k: The tide caves? I could get it back.
src: 'The tide caves? I could get it back.'

k: The tide caves are _full of things that bite_.
src: 'The tide caves are _full of things that bite_.'

k: Then you'd better come with me. Bring your bandages.
src: 'Then you\'d better come with me. Bring your bandages.'

k: Three things. One: we deliver the net first. Two: we're back before the ship comes in. Three: if you die, I'm telling your mother.
src: 'Three things. One: we deliver the net first. Two: we\'re back before the ship comes in. Three: if you die, I\'m telling your mother.'

k: Nana's Silver Gull
src: 'Nana\'s Silver Gull'

k: Find Nana Brisa's lost brooch in the Tide Caves, east of the village.
src: 'Find Nana Brisa\'s lost brooch in the Tide Caves, east of the village.'

k: Nana Brisa lost her silver gull brooch in the tide caves. Ilse and I are going to find it — after the net.
src: 'Nana Brisa lost her silver gull brooch in the tide caves. Ilse and I are going to find it — after the net.'

k: Tomorrow you'll both be grown. Sixteen.
src: 'Tomorrow you\'ll both be grown. Sixteen.'

k: I remember mine. My Crest burned so bright I couldn't see for an hour. Mender, same as Ilse will be — you mark my words.
src: 'I remember mine. My Crest burned so bright I couldn\'t see for an hour. Mender, same as Ilse will be — you mark my words.'

k: The tide caves are east along the shore road. Mind the pools.
src: 'The tide caves are east along the shore road. Mind the pools.'

k: Nana. Close your eyes and hold out your hand.
src: 'Nana. Close your eyes and hold out your hand.'

k: Oh, my silly gull. Look at you. Still missing your wing tip.
src: 'Oh, my silly gull. Look at you. Still missing your wing tip.'

k: Thank you, my darlings. Here — I was saving these for after the Kindling, but I think you've earned them early.
src: 'Thank you, my darlings. Here — I was saving these for after the Kindling, but I think you\'ve earned them early.'

k: She's going to cry.
src: 'She\'s going to cry.'

k: I am _not_. Off with you. Supper's at your mother's tonight, Wren, isn't it?
src: 'I am _not_. Off with you. Supper\'s at your mother\'s tonight, Wren, isn\'t it?'

k: We found the brooch. Nana cried. (Nana says she didn't.)
src: 'We found the brooch. Nana cried. (Nana says she didn\'t.)'

k: Ha! Brisa's knots. I'd know 'em in the dark.
src: 'Ha! Brisa\'s knots. I\'d know \'em in the dark.'

k: Here — for your trouble. Don't tell your mother I'm paying you in medicine. She'll think I'm sweet on her.
src: 'Here — for your trouble. Don\'t tell your mother I\'m paying you in medicine. She\'ll think I\'m sweet on her.'

k: Tide caves, is it? Careful. Tide's been strange all week. Pulls out further every morning, like the sea's holding its breath.
src: 'Tide caves, is it? Careful. Tide\'s been strange all week. Pulls out further every morning, like the sea\'s holding its breath.'

k: And take my old rod. A Halloway ought to fish. The dock end's good — face the water and give it a try.
src: 'And take my old rod. A Halloway ought to fish. The dock end\'s good — face the water and give it a try.'

k: A girl, out of the storm? The sea gives back strange things, Wren. Strange things.
src: 'A girl, out of the storm? The sea gives back strange things, Wren. Strange things.'

k: Mornin', Wren! Big day tomorrow, eh?
src: 'Mornin\', Wren! Big day tomorrow, eh?'

k: Brisa's got my net. I'd fetch it myself but my knees and her stairs are not on speaking terms.
src: 'Brisa\'s got my net. I\'d fetch it myself but my knees and her stairs are not on speaking terms.'

k: There — in the pool! Something silver.
src: 'There — in the pool! Something silver.'

k: Wren. The water's moving.
src: 'Wren. The water\'s moving.'

k: A silver gull. Missing the tip of one wing. That's it!
src: 'A silver gull. Missing the tip of one wing. That\'s it!'

k: Ilse... look at the back of the cave.
src: 'Ilse... look at the back of the cave.'

k: Is that... a crystal? It's _purple_. Crystals in these caves are blue.
src: 'Is that... a crystal? It\'s _purple_. Crystals in these caves are blue.'
